one_month_reasoning: One major scheduled event falls in the window: Q3 2026 results on Oct 28, 2026 (call at 1 PM ET), two trading days before the Oct 30 close (Oct 31 is a Saturday). Hyperscaler Q3 capex updates also land in late October. The guide is $9.3-9.4B in sales and $0.70-0.71 post-split EPS, and management said on the Q2 call that IT datacom should rise a further mid-teens percent sequentially in Q3. Amphenol beat the top of its guide in each of the last several quarters, so I expect a beat of about $0.76-0.80. The supervisor verified the earnings-day reactions over the last four prints: +3.6%, -12.2%, +3.2% and +4.5%. The press recaps (Nasdaq/Motley Fool, Chartmill) show the Jan-28 drop of 12-13% followed a beat whose Q1 guide implied a sequential EPS decline and disappointed after a run of broker upgrades. So the payoff is asymmetric: the beat is expected, and the downside comes from a soft Q4 guide or an uneven AI ramp. I lowered the centre from round 1. The model is 85% a lognormal at +1.5% with log-sd 0.115 plus 15% a guide-disappointment component at -7% with log-sd 0.16. That gives P(>=85.67) = 0.52, a median of about $86, and a fatter left tail than round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (60%): 2028E EPS $3.72 x 24.5x = $91.1, and FCF yield (40%): 2028E FCF $7.86B / 3.5% = $225B equity / 2.578B diluted post-split shares = $87.1. Both are Oct-2027 values on next-year numbers. Blended: $89.5.

methods.inputs: 2028E adj EPS $3.72 (2027 consensus $3.29 x 1.13) x 24.5x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: Cut from 15% in round 1. The supervisor established that every capex forecast it checked shows 2028 hyperscaler capex growth slowing sharply: Goldman +12% and UBS +6%. I take 13%, in the middle of the 10-15% range, because Amphenol's content gains, the CommScope optics business (doubled y/y in IT datacom per the Q2 call) and a 1.23 book-to-bill should let EPS grow somewhat faster than capex.

Today's price of $85.67 divided by 2027 consensus EPS of $3.29 gives 26.0x. I take 1.5 turns of derating as growth slows (25x in round 1), with the extra half turn for the GF Securities report of Kyber midplane share loss to Foxconn Interconnect. That report is unconfirmed, so it goes in the multiple, not in EPS.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2028E FCF $7.86B at a 3.5% equity FCF yield; 2.578B diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 2026 weighted diluted shares of 1,289.2M x 2 for the 2-for-1 split distributed Sept 2, 2026.

2028E EPS of $3.72 x 2.578B shares gives $9.59B of adjusted net income. I apply 82% FCF conversion: H1-26 ran at 65% because of a $1.18B working-capital build, while the long-run average is about 85%. Capex runs at the high end of 3-4% of sales.
Current market cap is about $221B. Against 2027E FCF of about $6.8B, that is a 3.1% yield. I widen it to 3.5% for slower growth by late 2027.

Total debt of $18.8B less $5.4B of cash and short-term investments at June 30, 2026. The supervisor rated the definitional gap with other agents immaterial (about $0.27 per share). It is already reflected in equity FCF after interest.

bear.story: AI/datacom orders digest in 2027 as hyperscaler capex growth slows toward UBS's path (+25% in 2027, +6% in 2028), and/or Foxconn Interconnect takes the major Kyber midplane share when Rubin Ultra ships. Book-to-bill falls below 1, 2028E EPS slips to about $3.1, and the multiple derates to about 18x, giving about $56.

base.story: Beats continue but EPS growth decelerates to about 13% in 2028, in line with the Goldman 2028 capex slowdown. Margins hold near 29-30%, and CommScope optics offsets some of the midplane share risk. EPS of $3.72 at 24.5x gives about $91.

bull.story: AI interconnect content (copper, optics and power) runs ahead of consensus, Kyber share holds up, and 2027 capex lands near Goldman's $1.2T. 2028E EPS reaches about $4.2 at 27x, giving about $114. I cut this from $123 because the 2028 capex slowdown caps both growth and the multiple.

thesis_break_reason: $59 sits just below the 2026 floor: closes of $59.58 (Mar 30) and $59.60 (May 19), and an intraday low of $59.01. It is about 18x 2027 consensus EPS of $3.29 and about 31% below today. Both earlier tests came from multiple compression (a conservative Q1 guide in January, then an AI-hardware rotation) while estimates kept rising. A close below that floor would most likely mean estimates are being cut: AI datacom book-to-bill below 1, a guide below consensus, a hyperscaler capex cut, or confirmed loss of the Kyber midplane socket. Other possible causes are margin damage from integration or a large adverse China tax ruling ($230M in payment notices already).

key_uncertainties: Durability of AI datacom demand (43% of sales, +63% organic in Q2-26). Every capex forecast checked shows 2028 hyperscaler capex growth slowing to single or low-double digits (Goldman +12%, UBS +6%).

Kyber midplane share: GF Securities reports that Foxconn Interconnect may have replaced APH as the major supplier. This is a single report, and management never comments on customers, so it may stay unresolved until the 2027 ramp.
Guide-driven reactions: the Jan-26 beat still fell 12% on a conservative guide, and the stock fell about 20% in three weeks after Q1.
How much of the 2026 margin step-up (29.8% adj OPM) is structural. Q2 included $80M of tariff recoveries, which management says will be immaterial going forward.
Multiple sustainability: about 26x 2027 consensus for a company whose growth is likely to halve.
Tax rate creep (adjusted ETR of 27%) and the China tax dispute; M&A execution and leverage.
reasoning: Everything is post-split (2-for-1, Sept 2, 2026). The round-1 primary-document base is unchanged, and EDGAR shows no new 8-K, 10-Q or Form 4 since the Sept 4 split 8-K. Q2-26 sales were $8.76B (+30% organic) with adj EPS of $1.35 pre-split against a $1.14-1.16 guide, on $10.7B of orders (book-to-bill 1.23). The Q3 guide is $0.70-0.71 post-split, with IT datacom guided up a further mid-teens percent sequentially. The round-1 filing details still hold: the $1.18B working-capital build, the China tax notices and routine Form 4 option sales. Supervisor findings I adopted: (1) 2028 capex growth slows sharply in every forecast checked (Goldman +12%, UBS +6%), so I cut 2028 EPS growth from 15% to 13% and the bull case from 28x/$4.4 to 27x/$4.2. (2) GF Securities reports Foxconn Interconnect may have displaced APH as the major Kyber midplane supplier. I confirmed the report exists (MSN and Intellectia headlines, analyst Alicia Xi) but could not confirm its date. Management at Citi (Sept 9) and on the Q2 call never addresses specific platforms and says only that 'the one constant is that there is more content'. So I treat it as an unconfirmed but credible risk: half a turn off the multiple and more bear weight (27%, from 25%). (3) Earnings reactions are asymmetric (Jan -12% on a beat with a soft guide), so I thinned the 1-month upside. Where I partly disagree: the Kyber report appears to be older news the stock has already absorbed (secondary coverage says APH fell about 5% on it), and CommScope's optics business and the company's multi-architecture positioning hedge it. So I do not cut EPS for it. Fair value is $89.5 (P/E $91.1, FCF $87.1), down from $92.2. Scenarios are bear $56 (27%), base $91 (50%) and bull $114 (23%), for a mean of about $87. The ladder is a mixture: 77% lognormal centred at $92 with sd 0.32, and 23% bear lognormal centred at $64 with sd 0.40. That gives a median of about $86 and P(>=86) = 0.50, in line with 46% realised vol and a fat left tail. Research was limited: Twelve Data estimates were paywalled, consensus came from one aggregator, and the Intellectia page returned 403.
